Folks — quick read from contracts/legal perspective. Couple of practical asks and suggested edits so we don't expose operational secrets or create open-ended inspection rights:

1) Pen-test clause — propose a "timeboxed and scoped" window: customer proposes 5 business days, Redwood provides a staging checklist and point of contact; tests must be non-destructive and pre-approved test plan is required. We should add a clause that any evidence requiring elevated access is redacted or replaced with attestations unless a separate NDA/inspection agreement is signed.

2) Audit rights — suggest replacing "full system access" with "reasonable access to evidence artifacts and sampled inspection sessions"; provide an evidence matrix that maps each audit item to the delivery method (SOC 2 report, log extracts, screenshots, attestation).

3) SLA/operational burden — add a line limiting evidence requests to a quarterly scheduled cadence for attachable artifacts, with emergency exceptions for incidents.

Attaching a quick redline and can formalize language this afternoon.

Thanks — attaching an initial evidence_matrix_clarity.xlsx and recommended operational patterns. Key security notes:

- SOC 2: Redwood can provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report and a short controls mapping for the environment that will host Clarity workloads (we'll indicate scope boundaries).
- Pen-test: we normally support a 3–5 business day window; for July 12–16 we'll require a staging checklist & test plan 10 business days prior. Tests must be executed against a dedicated staging instance or with safe-run restrictions (rate limits, API quotas disabled for long-running fuzzing).
- Evidence cadence: recommended baseline — quarterly artifact bundle (SOC2 report, access log extracts, compilation of relevant config snapshots) plus a 10-business-day turnaround for ad-hoc evidence requests that are scoped and mutually agreed.
- Sampling vs full inspection: propose sampled live sessions (screen share + recorded walk-through) for high-sensitivity artifacts instead of raw DB or HSM access.

I'll highlight which artifacts we can deliver directly vs those requiring redaction/attestation in the matrix. Happy to run a 30-minute technical sync with your security team this week.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
